topics.label: Lecture opening and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the session, connects it to prior practicals, and outlines the learning objectives.

topics.label: Tumor virology, cellular proto-oncogenes, and transformation assays
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how the historical study of transmissible tumor viruses led to the discovery of endogenous cellular proto-oncogenes and experimental assays for transformation.

topics.label: Classifications and mechanisms of oncogenes and tumor suppressor genes
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how cancer-promoting and tumor-suppressing mutations are defined, classified, and mechanistically exemplified through cell cycle checkpoints and gene dosage effects.

topics.label: Mechanisms and consequences of sequence and chromosomal genetic instability
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address the distinct molecular defects in DNA repair, replication, and mitotic chromosome segregation that generate genomic instability in cancer cells.

topics.label: Multistep tumor progression, hereditary predispositions, and tumor maintenance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how sequential genetic alterations drive cancer progression over time in both sporadic disease and inherited cancer syndromes.

topics.label: Closing remarks and recommended reading
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the session, suggests supplementary reading, and previews the upcoming lecture topic.
